messages.subject: Dates in R studio
parts:
I have a data set that was showing my three date variables as factors.

So i used the R code below to convert those columns to dates:
Broiler[,"CloseWeek"] = as.Date(Broiler[,"CloseWeek"]) 
Broiler[,"KillDate"] = as.Date(Broiler[,"KillDate"])
Broiler[,"HatchDate"] = as.Date(Broiler[,"HatchDate"]) 
date <- as.Date("11-03-2015", format = "%m/%d/%Y")

The first 2 lines "worked", except now the dates are extremely messy- see attached screenshot.
The code did not work for HatchDate - it is still coded as a "factor" in R, but at least it has dates.
The fourth line of code didn't seem to help.

Suggestions?
  • should i leave the dates as they were, even though R thinks they are "factors"
  • is there another way to fix dates in R that I am missing?
Thanks!
Laura

parts:
as.Date(), by default tries to convert dates assuming their format is Y/M/D. That’s why this sometimes works but badly - “9/9/13”, is interpreted as September 13, 0009, as opposed to September 9, 2013. With a date like “11/27/13”, it fails, because there is no month 27. Since ALL the HatchDate column values fail, it returns an error, but for the other columns it just returns NA.

So you need to do as Brandon suggested: put a format="%m/%d/%y" argument into each of your as.Date() calls.

The shorthand codes for date formats can all be found in ?strptime, and Bonnie’s tutorial also goes into some detail on how the lubridate package has some convenience functions for this.
